behavior: Persist workflow state to a PostgreSQL checkpointer at every node boundary of the agent-harness workflow so an interrupted run can be reloaded from its latest durable checkpoint.
nonGoals: No resume orchestration or interrupt handling (HAR-004-T01)
No adapter, transport or evidence code path changes
No planning, requirement or catalog edits
commands: STRUCTILE_DEV_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE="$PWD/.local/postgres-password" docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.test.yaml up -d --wait postgres

STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_HOST=127.0.0.1 STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PORT=55432 STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_USER=structile STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_DB=structile STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE="$PWD/.local/postgres-password" node --test packages/agent-harness/test/*.test.ts
notes: protectedTests HAR-002 is the catalog suite covering HAR-003, HAR-004, HAR-005, HAR-006 and HAR-010 (verification/test-catalog.json); per CP-002's ruling this suite will be re-cut into per-requirement sub-suites, and this contract cites the current catalog entry pending that amendment. runnerDigest is the attested G0 runner image pending a G1 runner attestation; task-ready v1 does not verify runnerDigest or testSourceDigest. testSourceDigest is the oracle-input digest of structile-conformance main 46c8cf99cbac5d0c87729e08db20bbadbe2bacd0, computed by calling the runner's own runnerDigests() in src/evidence.ts directly rather than invented. @structile/agent-harness currently declares zero runtime dependencies; persisting checkpoints to PostgreSQL needs a client library, so allowedPaths adds packages/agent-harness/package.json plus root package-lock.json (listed in generatedPaths, excluded from line-count as a reproducible lockfile companion per the schema). compose.yaml's postgres service publishes no host port and sits only on the internal `data` network, so a host-run `node --test` process has no route to it; the compose step now layers the repo-root test-only override compose.test.yaml (`-f compose.yaml -f compose.test.yaml`), which publishes postgres on 127.0.0.1:55432 without changing compose.yaml's own security posture. Tests reach PostgreSQL via STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_HOST=127.0.0.1 and STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PORT=55432 (extending the STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_HOST/PORT convention already established for foundation-health), plus STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_USER/STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_DB (fixed values from compose.yaml) and STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE pointed at the same local secret file used to bring the container up, so the actual password never needs to be read out-of-band; all four are set explicitly on the `node --test` command line. This sequence was executed end-to-end against a live Docker daemon on 2026-08-25: compose up -d --wait postgres over the override reached Healthy, and a host client authenticated to 127.0.0.1:55432 as structile/structile and ran SELECT 1 successfully before teardown. Separately, runnerDigest carries the attested G0 runner image digest because no G1 runner digest exists yet: the protected G1 workflow builds the image fresh from Containerfile and computes imageDigest from the built image, and conformance src/ and verification/ have grown substantially since the G0 authority commit, so the G1 image's digest will differ. task-ready v1 verifies neither digest, but readiness against a real protected run requires the pinned runner to match, so this field is a placeholder to be re-pinned to the first attested G1 runner digest. Every task contract merged to date carries the same placeholder. 2026-08-26 touch-up: protectedTests re-pointed to HARD-001 per the CP-002 re-cut now merged into verification/test-catalog.json, testSourceDigest re-pinned at structile-conformance main 20ca0d3, and baseCommit bumped to structile main 5dda0d5, retiring the stale-baseCommit task-ready violations this contract previously carried.
